communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Enforcement and Complaint Records Concerning Hotels
communications.communication:
Dear Records Access Officer:

Under the New York Freedom of Information Law (Public Officers Law, Article 6), I request copies of the records described below. Unless a different period is stated, the period for each item is January 1, 2021 through the date this request is processed. Schedule A, below, lists the hotel addresses referred to in several items. Where an item refers to "a hotel," it means any hotel in Manhattan, including but not limited to those on Schedule A.

For any item that the Commission maintains in a database, case management system, or spreadsheet, an export of the responsive records from that system, with the fields identified in the item, satisfies the request. I am not asking for individual paper summonses or complaint forms where a system export exists. I have obtained 311 complaint data from NYC Open Data and am not requesting the 311 records themselves, except as stated in item 1.

Publicly available 311 data shows clusters of complaints in the category "Driver Complaint - Non Passenger" at the 58th Street entrance of the Four Seasons Hotel (32 East 58th Street, including eleven complaints filed on October 30, 2025), at 7 West 60th Street adjacent to the Mandarin Oriental, at the Park Lane Hotel (36 Central Park South), and at The New Yorker (481 Eighth Avenue), with dispositions indicating that the Commission issued notices, obtained guilty pleas, and scheduled OATH hearings. Several items below are intended to capture the complaint narratives, complainant types, summonses, and dispositions associated with those clusters. I have also received information that Commission enforcement personnel were present at the Four Seasons Hotel during the summer of 2026.

Records requested

1. Complaints received directly by the Commission, other than through 311, that reference a hotel, hotel doorman, hotel concierge, hotel bell staff, or a payment, tip, kickback, "vig," or commission paid by a driver, base, or for-hire vehicle company to hotel staff in connection with passenger referrals, airport trips, or vehicle dispatch, including complaints from passengers, drivers, and licensed bases. Fields: date received, complaint source or type, location, category, disposition. This item also includes, for any complaint whose incident location is a Schedule A address, whether received directly or referred from 311, the complaint narrative or description as recorded by the Commission and the complainant type (passenger, driver, base, hotel employee, or other) where recorded. 

2. Summonses and notices of violation issued for any incident located at a Schedule A address or within one block of it. Fields: date, incident location, rule or section cited, licensee type (driver, vehicle, or base), disposition. If the Commission's system does not support a proximity search, an export limited to incidents at the Schedule A addresses satisfies this item.

3. Decisions of the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings, or of the Commission, resolving any summons or notice of violation responsive to item 2.

4. Records of any enforcement operation, detail, sweep, or undercover program conducted at or directed at a hotel from January 1, 2023 through the date this request is processed, including June through September 2026: operation plans, deployment orders, and after-action or results summaries, whether or not summonses were issued.

5. Records maintained by the Enforcement Bureau, including the Uniformed Services Bureau, reflecting the assignment or deployment of enforcement personnel at or to a hotel from January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed, including tour or post assignment sheets, daily deployment plans, detail orders, and overtime authorizations that reference a hotel.

6. Any list, map, bulletin, briefing, or analysis maintained by the Enforcement Bureau or any intelligence, analytics, or planning unit that identifies hotels, hotel curbs, or "hot spots" for illegal solicitation, unlicensed pickups, or hustling in Manhattan, from January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed.

7. Records showing the location of enforcement stops, summonses, or patrol posts at a Schedule A address from January 1, 2023 through the date this request is processed, including stop logs, summons geolocation data, and patrol or post lists.

8. Records of complaints or tips referred to the Enforcement Bureau for follow-up that reference a hotel, and the disposition of each referral.

9. Records showing whether any Schedule A address has been designated in the Commission's systems as an enforcement priority location, hot spot, or similar designation, and the date of each designation.

10. The Commission's 2026 driver survey described in the Commissioner's July 2026 letter to licensees: the survey instrument, the tabulated results, and any free-text responses that mention hotels, doormen, concierges, or solicitation or hustling at locations other than airports.

SUBJECT: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: Vector Control Manifests, GPS Telemetry & Internal Communications (Lot 802 / Square 5812)

To the D.C. Health (DOH) FOIA Officer and Carl Filler:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am submitting an expedited demand for public records concerning the Department's emergency response to a documented biological and structural hazard located at the artificial retention basin on Lot 802, Square 5812 (adjacent to 1488-1500 Morris Rd SE).

On Saturday, September 12, 2026, I filed an urgent code-enforcement complaint with D.C. Health demanding immediate vector abatement (larviciding) and emergency fencing for this toxic, stagnant overflow pond. On Monday, September 14, 2026, at 10:00 AM, DOH Chief of Staff Carl Filler confirmed in writing that a D.C. Health vector control team had visited the site and treated the pond with a long-acting larvicide. Mr. Filler, however, failed to address the simultaneous demand for emergency safety fencing to mitigate the attractive nuisance and drowning hazard under D.C. Code § 6-801.
To ensure total transparency regarding the Department's official recognition and remediation of this site, I am formally requesting copies of the following records generated between Saturday, September 12, 2026, and the date this request is processed:

1. Certified Work Orders & Chemical Manifests: The official D.C. Health field inspection report, technician work order, and the specific EPA registration number/manifest for the 6-month larvicide deployed at Lot 802, Square 5812, on or prior to September 14, 2026.
2. GPS/AVL Vehicle Telemetry: All GPS coordinates, Automatic Vehicle Location (AVL) data, and dispatch logs for the specific D.C. Health or District Vector Control vehicle that visited the 1400-1500 blocks of Morris Rd SE to conduct this treatment.
3. Internal Communications & Frantic Forwarding (Carl Filler): Digital telemetry confirms that my September 12 emergency demand was opened and/or forwarded internally over 40 times on the morning of September 14, just prior to Mr. Filler's response. I demand all emails, internal memorandums, Microsoft Teams chat transcripts, and forwarded messages sent from, received by, or CC'd to Carl Filler regarding Lot 802, Morris Rd SE, vector abatement, or Fred Gamble during this timeframe.4. Interagency Coordination & Fencing Refusal: Any communications between Carl Filler, Director Ayanna Bennett, or D.C. Health staff and representatives from the Department of Energy & Environment (DOEE), Department of Buildings (DOB), or District Department of Transportation (DDOT) regarding the jurisdictional responsibility of the pond, or the justification for refusing to mandate emergency safety fencing around the hazard.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA / Archival Record Request: FAA Great Lakes Region NTAP/PDARS Radar Logs (September 11, 2001)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request access to and copies of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Great Lakes Region Air Traffic Control records preserved within the 9/11 Commission files or general FAA record groups (Record Group 237).

Specifically, request includes:

National Track Analysis Program (NTAP) or Performance Data Analysis Reporting System (PDARS) automated radar track data extractions covering the airspace sectors controlling eastern Montana, North Dakota, Minnesota, and Wisconsin between 12:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC on September 11, 2001.

Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC) Command Center Logs and military coordinator logbooks from the Minneapolis ARTCC (ZMP) for flights utilizing refueling tracks AR-310 or AR-610 during the national airspace ground stop window.

Sector voice recording logs or transcripts for the ZMP sectors handling military tactical traffic with callsigns "CLEAN" [01-10], "AMC 319", or military fighter tracks matching Lt. Col. Gibney's mission trajectory.

REQUEST FOR NEWS MEDIA STATUS & FEE WAIVER

1. Representative of the News Media Status

I request that I be categorized as a representative of the news media for fee assessment purposes under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II) and 32 C.F.R. § 286.12.

I am an independent journalist conducting an investigative historical report regarding the air defense and aerial refueling infrastructure in operation on September 11, 2001.

The requested records are not sought for commercial use. They will be used purely in my editorial capacity for a forthcoming, deep-dive investigative feature to be published on critic.markciubal.com. This platform regularly publishes analytical, data-driven investigative journalism regarding historical aviation, military records, and public safety data.

As a modern independent publisher, I perform the traditional journalistic functions of gathering information, exercising editorial judgment to analyze and synthesize raw data, and distributing the finalized work to the public.

2. Request for a Public Interest Fee Waiver

Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii), I request a complete waiver of all search, duplication, and review fees because disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest.

Understanding Government Operations: The requested FAA radar extractions and military squadron flight logs shed direct light on the operations, response times, and coordination of the Department of Defense and the Federal Aviation Administration during a critical turning point in national security history.

Significant Contribution to Public Understanding: There is an active, ongoing historical debate regarding the precise timelines, geographic ranges, and interception metrics achieved on September 11, 2001. The public currently lacks access to these raw data-extraction logs and squadron records. Publishing a synthesized, mathematically verified analysis of these flight envelopes on critic.markciubal.com will significantly inform public understanding by replacing administrative ambiguity with verifiable physical data.

No Commercial Interest: I have no commercial motive. This investigation is entirely for independent educational, historical, and journalistic purposes.

If this request for news media status or a fee waiver is denied, please notify me immediately before incurring any fees exceeding $25.00.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Mark Daniel Ciubal

4a. Flock networks shared with the Department
4b. Networks that the Department is sharing

6. The locations and orientations of all ALPR cameras, including but not limited to Flock ALPR cameras, deployed by NFTA Transit PD

7. All versions of the applicable policies for the deployment of automated license plate recognition cameras/readers/systems, as well as for usage, storage and sharing of any data obtained by using such systems.

8. 9. 13. The list of active authorized users with access to the ALPR system and records of additions to or removals from that list, from January 1, 2020 to the date this request is processed.

Please provide records in their original electronic, machine readable format. For example, please provide csv or spreadsheet files where applicable.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter.

Sincerely,

Scott Conway

title: Obama Presidential Library: USAID Telecommunications Development & Infrastructure Security in Georgia and Armenia (2011–2012)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Obama Presidential Library: USAID Telecommunications Development & Infrastructure Security in Georgia and Armenia (2011–2012)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I. Request Scope & Description of Records

I request copies of all records created, received, or maintained within National Security Council (NSC) channels, or transmitted to/from NSC staff by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) or its Bureau for Europe and Eurasia (E&E), between April 6, 2011, and December 31, 2012, concerning telecommunications development, critical infrastructure security, and internet connectivity in Georgia and Armenia following the April 6, 2011, fiber-optic line severance outside Tbilisi.

For context, an elderly woman collecting copper in the hills outside of Tbilisi in April of 2011 disabled Armenia's internet connectivity:
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/apr/06/georgian-woman-cuts-web-access

Specifically, this request includes:

● NSC briefing memoranda, situation reports, and correspondence discussing the April 2011 fiber-optic severance and its effect on Armenian internet connectivity.

● Correspondence between NSC staff (e.g., the Senior Director for Russian and Eurasian Affairs) and USAID's Bureau for Europe and Eurasia regarding telecommunications sector resilience, broadband access, or critical infrastructure security in Georgia and Armenia.

● Interagency or bilateral correspondence discussing regional reliance on single-channel transit corridors (such as Armenian routes transiting Georgia or Iran).

● Any records reflecting U.S. Embassy Tbilisi or U.S. Embassy Yerevan reporting on the incident that was forwarded to or discussed within NSC channels.

II. Suggested Search Terms & Parameters

To assist your search, please query electronic and paper systems (including text collections, briefing books, and email databases) using the following keyword clusters:
● "USAID Georgia" OR "USAID Armenia"
● "Hayastan Shakarian" OR "ჰაიასტან შაქარიანი" OR "Հայաստան Շաքարյան"
● "telecommunications infrastructure" OR "Georgian telecommunications infrastructure" OR "Armenian telecommunications infrastructure" OR "South Caucasus telecommunications infrastructure"
● "broadband accessibility" OR "digital connectivity"
● "network security" OR critical "infrastructure protection"
● "Caucasus Online" OR "fiber optic" OR "internet blackout"


III. Date Range

The records sought span from April 6, 2011, through December 31, 2012.

IV. Format Request

I request that any responsive records be provided electronically via email or on digital storage media or, ideally, simply uploaded online in the spirit of the Obama library's "digital-first" ethos. 

V. Withholdings & Segregability

If any portion of this request is denied or withheld pursuant to statutory exemptions under the FOIA or Presidential Records Act, please specify the exemption(s) applied to each withheld record, provide a Vaughn index itemizing the basis for each withholding, and release all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions. 

Thank you for your assistance with this request. I look forward to receiving your response within the statutory time frame. I appreciate the work that the Obama Presidential Library does each and every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
